operations.title: The integral norm relation defines a canonical two-periodic complex
operations.statement: For a finite group G of order d over a commutative ring R, norm multiplication T satisfies T^2=dT, hence alternating T and d-T gives a two-periodic complex. Its norm-side homology is I/(dI+R(d*1-nu_G)), where I is the augmentation ideal. It vanishes after d is inverted and specializes in characteristic dividing d to I/(k nu_G) of dimension d-2.
operations.scope: Regular group-ring correspondence only; no physical relative-chain realization.

operations.title: Integral C2/C3 specialization control
operations.procedure: For C2, d*1-nu=1-g generates the augmentation ideal, so the integral norm-side homology vanishes. For C3, in the rank-two augmentation basis the extra relation is the diagonal vector modulo 3, leaving Z/3.
operations.expected_result: C2 gives zero and C3 gives Z/3; failure of either quotient calculation falsifies the claimed formula.
